questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in the national income?

options.text: Income received by a person as a donation
Income received by a household for the use of their entrepreneurial skill
Income received by a person for the use of his capital
Income received by a household for the use of their land

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Income received by a person as a donation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Income received by a person as a donation** is excluded from the **national income** because it does not represent any productive activity or contribution to the economy.
 
• National income is calculated based on the value of goods and services produced within a country during a specific time period, and donations are considered **voluntary transfers** rather than income earned through economic activities.
 
• Donations are typically categorized as **unilateral transfers**, which include gifts, grants, or aid, and do not reflect the country's economic productivity.
 
• Examples of unilateral transfers include **charitable contributions, foreign aid, and remittances**. These are excluded because they are not tied to the production of goods or services.
 
• The exclusion of donations ensures that the national income reflects only **, thereby accurately measuring the country's economic performance.
 
• This distinction is crucial in economic analysis to differentiate between earned income** and transfers that do not result from productive activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Income received by a household for the use of their entrepreneurial skill**__

 __
 
• This income is included in the national income as it represents **payment for services** related to entrepreneurship, such as managing businesses, organizing production, or innovating.
 
• It is considered part of the **factor income** earned through productive activity and contributes to the economy.
 
• Entrepreneurial income falls under the category of **profit**, which is a key component of national income calculation.
 
 
 
• **Income received by a person for the use of his capital**__
 __
 
• This income represents **interest payments** or returns on investments and is included in the national income because it is a reward for the productive use of capital.
 
• Capital income contributes to the economic output and reflects the **monetary value of resources** used in production.
 
 
 
• **Income received by a household for the use of their land**__
 
 
• This income is categorized as **rent**, which is included in national income as it represents payment for the use of a productive resource.
 
• Land is a factor of production, and the income derived from its use is considered part of the economic activity that contributes to the national income.

questions.question: What is personal income?

options.text: The income earned by individuals and households after taxes and other deductions
The total income earned by businesses and corporations in an economy
The income earned by individuals through their own business or self-employment
The total income earned by individuals and households before taxes and other deductions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the total income earned by individuals and households before taxes and other deductions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Personal income** is the total income earned by individuals and households before taxes and other deductions.
 
• It includes wages, salaries, bonuses, social security benefits, dividends, interest, and rental income.
 
• Personal income is a measure of the **financial resources available to individuals and households for spending and saving**.
 
• It is an important economic indicator used to assess the economic well-being of the population and to predict future consumer spending.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disposable income** is the **income available to individuals and households after taxes and other deductions**.
 
• It represents the amount of money that can be spent or saved according to personal preferences.
 
• Personal income and disposable income are key metrics in macroeconomic analysis and policy-making.
 
• Understanding the levels and trends of personal income helps in assessing the overall economic health and planning for fiscal policies.

questions.question: Why are intermediate goods NOT included in the calculation of national income?

options.text: Including intermediate goods would result in double counting.
Intermediate goods are not produced within the country's borders.
Including intermediate goods would decrease the value of national income.
Intermediate goods are not important for measuring economic activity.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Including intermediate goods would result in double counting.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Including intermediate goods would result in double counting.** This is because intermediate goods are used in the production of final goods and services. Including them separately in national income calculations would mean counting them multiple times.
 
• National income aims to measure the** value of final goods and services** produced within a country. Intermediate goods are already accounted for in the value of these final goods.
 
• By excluding intermediate goods, economists ensure that national income reflects the true economic activity and avoids inflation of the GDP figures.
 
• Examples of intermediate goods include raw materials, components, and other inputs used in the production process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• National income is a crucial indicator of a country's economic performance and is used for comparing economic activity over time and between different economies.
 
• It includes measures such as **Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Gross National Product (GNP), and Net National Product (NNP)**.
 
• The exclusion of intermediate goods helps in avoiding the overestimation of national income and provides a clear picture of a nation's economic output.
 
• Intermediate goods can be transformed into final goods, which are then sold to consumers or used in further production processes.

questions.question: Factor cost is also known as:
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'input cost'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Understanding Factor Cost:**

 
 
• Factor cost refers to the cost of the factors of production used in the production of goods and services.
 
• It includes all costs associated with the inputs used in the production process, such as labor, raw materials, and capital.
 
• In economics, factor cost is often termed as input cost because it represents the expenses incurred in obtaining the necessary inputs for production.
 
• Factor cost does not include taxes and other levies that may be added to the final price of a product.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Comparison with Other Costs:**

 
 
• **Option 1 (Market Cost):**

 
 
• Market cost includes all expenses related to producing and selling a good or service, including profit margins, and is not synonymous with factor cost.
 
 
 
• **Option 2 (Ex-factory Cost):**
 
 
• This term refers to the cost of goods at the factory gate, excluding transportation and distribution costs, and does not equate to factor cost.
 
 
 
• **Option 4 (Output Cost):**
 
 
• Output cost refers to the total cost of producing a particular level of output, including fixed and variable costs, which may extend beyond just factor costs.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Understanding factor cost is crucial for analyzing production costs and determining pricing strategies in business.
 
• It serves as a foundational concept in economic theories relating to production, cost analysis, and pricing mechanisms.
 
• Recognizing the difference between factor cost and other cost types helps businesses and economists make informed decisions regarding resource allocation and production efficiency.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about transfer payments in relation to personal income?

options.text: Transfer payments are included in personal income.
Transfer payments have no impact on personal income.
Transfer payments are included in personal income only for businesses.
Transfer payments are excluded from personal income

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**transfer payments are included in personal income**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Transfer payments are included in personal income.** This means that when calculating personal income, transfer payments such as social security benefits, unemployment compensation, and welfare payments are added.
 
• Transfer payments are a significant component of personal income, especially for individuals who rely on government assistance.
 
• These payments are not in exchange for goods or services provided and do not represent earned income, but they still contribute to the overall personal income of individuals.
 
• Including transfer payments in personal income provides a more comprehensive understanding of an individual's total income resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Personal income** is the total income received by individuals and households before paying personal taxes.
 
• It includes wages, salaries, bonuses, social security benefits, dividends, interest, rental income, and transfer payments.
 
• Transfer payments are typically funded through taxation and are aimed at redistributing wealth to provide financial support to individuals in need.
 
• Understanding the role of transfer payments in personal income is crucial for analyzing economic policies and their impact on income distribution and poverty alleviation.

questions.question: Which among the following is included in the gross domestic product?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Sales of final goods.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Sales of final goods are included in the gross domestic product.**
 
• **GDP or Gross Domestic Product** is the total value or market value of all the goods and services in a year in a country's economy. Intermediate goods are not included while calculating GDP.
 
• **GDP:**
 
 
• GDP's full form is **Gross Domestic Product**. It is evaluated regularly to account for changing production structure, relative prices, and better recording of economic activities.
 
• Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the total money value of** final goods and services** produced in the economic territories of a country in a given year.
 
• Non-monetary goods and services (e.g. cooking by a housewife) are not included in GDP calculation.

questions.question: Which of the following is included in the estimation of Gross National Product?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sale of new shirts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross National Product (GNP)** is the total market value of all final goods and services produced by a country's residents in a given time period, regardless of where the production takes place.
 
• The **sale of new shirts** is included in GNP because it represents the production of a **final good** within the economy.
 
• GNP includes the value of **newly produced goods and services**, which are counted at their market value to avoid double counting.
 
• The production of new goods like shirts contributes to the **economic output** and reflects the labor, capital, and other inputs used in manufacturing.
 
• It excludes intermediate goods to prevent **double-counting**, which ensures that only the value of final goods is included.
 
• This type of transaction adds to the overall economic activity and is measured as part of the GNP of a country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pension payments**__

 __
 
• Pension payments are **transfer payments**, meaning they are not made in exchange for goods or services. Hence, they are not included in the GNP.
 
• Transfer payments do not reflect current production or economic activity but are rather a redistribution of income.
 
 
 
• **Sale of securities**__
 __
 
• The sale of securities (like stocks and bonds) is considered a financial transaction and does not represent the production of goods or services.
 
• Such transactions are excluded from GNP as they do not contribute to the economic output.
 
 
 
• **Sale of used cars**__
 
 
• The sale of used cars is not included in GNP because it does not represent the production of new goods or services.
 
• Only the value of new production is counted in GNP to avoid double-counting the value of goods produced in previous years.
